manufacturer_data.description: 0xBE99 — Shenzhen ELK mesh/broadcast family. Device-side advertisements use this company ID; if data[1]==0x40 then data[2] is a device-type ID (the app maps it to a display name). Names start with ELK-/MELK-/ELBU- or an OEM variant; the vendor app itself ignores names starting with ELKP.

device.name: LotusLamp X BLE LED Controller
device.notes:
Addressable RGB LED strip/lamp controllers designed against the LotusLamp X app (com.szelk.ledlamppro, analyzed v5.19.08), sold under the ELK-/MELK-/ELBU- advertised-name families and many OEM rebrands. BLE-only: the app declares no Wi-Fi/UDP usage anywhere. Same 9-byte 7E..EF E1 frame family as elk-bledom-led-strip.yaml and wl-smartled-pixel-strips.yaml (keep the three in sync), but a wider opcode set and two extra control paths (advertising broadcast + mesh).
TRANSPORTS (all BLE, no classic pairing, no bonding, no auth):
  1. GATT connection (primary): service 0xFFF0, write 0xFFF3
     (write-without-response), notify 0xFFF4. On connect the app also
     reads standard Device Information characteristics (2A24/2A25/
     2A26/2A27/2A29) and Battery Level (2A19).
  2. Connectionless broadcast: the PHONE advertises manufacturer data
     the lamp listens for — company ID 0xE190 (57744) for E1-family
     devices, 0xE290 (58000) for E2-family. Payload:
     <seq> 13 01 BE <9-byte E1 command frame> <sum16 of all preceding
     bytes, little-endian>.
  3. Mesh broadcast: company ID 0xBE99 (48793), 22-byte packet:
     [0]=protoVer(2) [1]=1 [2]=deviceType [3:4]=phone-uuid BE
     [5]=familyId [6]=roomId [7]=groupId [8]=0x40 [9]=cmd
     [10:14]=params (pad 0xFF) [15:18]=0 [19]=packetNo
     [20:21]=CRC16 LE. The CRC is a BLE CRC-24 core (poly 0x100065B,
     init 0x555555, fully reflected) seeded with the LE manufacturer
     ID bytes, truncated to 16 bits. Group provisioning (familyId /
     roomId / groupId assignment) is only partially traced — MEDIUM.

E1 FRAME (classic, 9 bytes): 7E <len> <cmd> <p0> <p1> <p2> <p3> <p4> EF. <len> is 4 for BRIGHTNESS, 6 for DATA_TIME, else 7 in the app — but the firmware appears NOT to validate it strictly (the published lotus-lamp library used 7 for brightness and 4 for speed against a live MELK-OA10 with success). Treat <len> as informational; emit the app-canonical values from the commands below. Unused params pad 0xFF; the byte before EF defaults 0x00 (0x10 in the app's color frame).
E2 FRAME: 8E <len+1> <cmd> <params...> — variable length, no trailer. E3 FRAME: 2E <cmd> <params pad 0xFF> 2F — 16 bytes when cmd < 0x10, else 128 bytes. E2/E3 are used by other device families sharing this app (pixel strips, curtain/TV backlight devices); the E1 commands below are what an ELK-/MELK- lamp needs. A niche third family uses 55 A5 05 03 R G B FF FF FF-style frames (ignore unless met in the field).
ENCRYPTED VARIANT (ELK-*): devices whose advertised name has '*' as the 4th character instead of '-' (e.g. "ELK*...") run firmware that requires an obfuscated E1 frame for ON_OFF / MODE / BRIGHTNESS only. The plaintext frame is wrapped in an 0xAA..0x55 envelope and expanded to a 21-byte blob: bytes 0-8 are the plaintext XOR a keystream where keystream[i] = ((rnd[i]*27) ^ (rnd[(i+3)%12]+55) ^ (rnd[(i+7)%12]>>2) ^ (i*85)) & 0xFF over 12 random bytes rnd[]; bytes 9-20 are the 12 random bytes each XOR a repeating 16-byte preset key hardcoded in the app. This is toy XOR obfuscation, not AES (no AES/DES exists in the app's BLE path); the preset key is recoverable from the app by anyone. Existence noted per clean-room rules — key bytes intentionally not reproduced here.
DISCOVERY: service UUID 0xFFF0 is the reliable signal. Advertised name prefixes accepted by the app: ELK-, MELK-, ELBU- plus OEM variants HX6-, HCW-, BYC-, SHY-, MHRS-, THUNDEROBOT, "LED LIGHT STRIP", "LED Constellation Lights" and more. The app's BLE scanner DROPS devices whose name starts with "ELKP" and reads company-ID 0xBE99 manufacturer data: if data[1]==0x40, data[2] is a device-type ID it maps to a synthesized display name.
OPCODE MAP (cmd byte, hex): BRIGHTNESS 01, SPEED 02, MODE 03, ON_OFF 04, COLOR 05, MIC 06, MIC_ON_OFF 07, PHONE_MAI_RHYTHM 08, CUSTOM 0A, SET_SERIAL_PORT_BAUD_RATE 0B, TIMER 0D, HUMAN_SENSOR 12, LIGHT_SENSOR/BIND 13, SET_GROUP 14, FAVORITE 15, AUTO_CAROUSEL 16, SPILED_PARAM 21, SYMPHONY_COLLAPSE_MODE 22, SET_COPPER_WIRE_MODE 23, GET_PROTECT_CODE 24, SET_SCENE 31, START/SET/END_SCENE_DIY 32/33/34, GET_SCENE_DIY 36, GET_SET_SCENE_DIY_FOR_LIGHT_STRIP 37, SET_ENHANCED_SCENE_DIY 39, FIRES_* 40/41/42, READY_UPDATE 43, SET_EFFECT 50, SET_ANIMATION_EFFECT 51, SET_SEND_STATIC_IMAGE 52, SET_DYNAMIC_IMAGE 53, SET_DYNAMIC_IMAGE_DIY 54, SET_DYNAMIC_IMAGE_TEXT 55, SET_RHYTHM_STYLE 56, SET_RHYTHM_DATA 57, SET_POINT_COLOR 58, SET_BACKGROUND_IMAGE 59, SET_TEXT_COLOR 5A, SET_TEXT_GRADIENT_IMAGE 5B, SET_BACKGROUND_COLOR 5C, SET_BACKGROUND_SWITCH 5D, SET_TEXT_COLOR_SWITCH 5E, SET_DIY_IMAGE 60, SET_RHYTHM_DIRECTION 61, SET_RHYTHM_FOLD 62, SET_MIRROR_IMAGE 63, SET_CURTAIN_DIY_DATA_MORE/SET_TV_OPEN 64, SET_MODE_STYLE/ SET_SURROUND 65, READ_TV_POINT 66, SET_SYNC_CODE 72, SET_OFF_TIME 76, MONO_STROBE 77, MONO_FLOW 78, STOP_PLAY 80, SEQ 81, TIMER_SWITCH 82, DATA_TIME 83, INFO 84, SET_RESTORE_FACTORY 87, PAIRED_HOST 88, MULTI_TIMER_SETTING 89, MULTI_TIMER_READ 8A, LOCK_HOST 8C, TWO_CH_CAR_LIGHT_LAMP_SELECT 8E, TWO_CH_CAR_LIGHT_ANIMATION C0, MESH_CONTROL_SINGLE C1, MESH_CHANGE_GROUP C2, MESH_ADD_GROUP C3, SET_CLEAR_PAIR C4, SET_DEVICE_CLEAR_PAIR C5, SET_FLOWING_SWITCH D6, SET_BLE_SETTING D7, SET_MOTOR_SETTING D8, SET_DEVICE E1, SET_APP_TYPE EA, DIY_FUNCTION FD, COLORFUL_SYNC_LAMP_PENETRATE FF.
PRIVACY: the app uploads device stats/telemetry to http://lotus.elkled.com:8082 (endpoints /api/profile/allowupload and /api/info/add) and self-updates from https://www.elkble.com. The lamp itself never needs the network — a replacement client talking GATT keeps the device fully local. Firmware updates, if offered, ride the GATT channel (READY_UPDATE 0x43 + image opcodes 0x52-0x54 in 500-byte packets); no DFU service or firmware file URLs exist in the app.
CONFIDENCE: service/characteristic UUIDs and the 9-byte E1 frame HIGH — the app's protocol code matches the independently reverse engineered wporter82/lotus-lamp-python (pypi.org/project/lotus-lamp), which is LIVE-TESTED on a MELK-OA10 unit; that library corroborates the color/brightness/speed/mode/power commands below. The 213-mode animation table (modes 0-212) is HIGH per the same library. E2/E3 framing, the broadcast/mesh packet layouts and the ELK-* obfuscation scheme are static-analysis only — MEDIUM, verify against live capture. FFF4 notification payload semantics (state echoes in 7E..EF framing) are unmapped — needs a live capture.

credentials.notes: No auth on classic firmware; anything in radio range can connect and issue commands. The ELK-* encrypted variant adds XOR obfuscation with an app-embedded preset key — obfuscation, not access control (the key is recoverable from the app). Physical proximity remains the only real barrier.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear. The app exposes a SET_RESTORE_FACTORY opcode (0x87) in the E1 frame family, but its exact frame layout and effect are untested — treat as unverified. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the lamp holds only one BLE link and another central is still attached.

steps.action: Remove power for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Lamp advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: Scan for the 0xFFF0 service UUID (or an ELK-/MELK-/ELBU- name), connect, and write 9-byte E1 command frames to characteristic 0xFFF3. Classic (non-ELK-*) firmware needs no initialization sequence. Subscribe to 0xFFF4 for state echoes.

steps.action: Scan for the 0xFFF0 service UUID and connect.
Optionally subscribe to 0xFFF4 notifications, then write E1 frames to 0xFFF3.

setup.notes: No provisioning. The lamp advertises when powered and accepts a connection from any central — no account, no pairing PIN, no credential exchange. Confidence medium: no live capture in this repo; the flow is corroborated by the independently tested lotus-lamp-python library, which simply scans, connects and writes.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds the lamp to an owner or network, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. The lamp accepts a single BLE connection at a time — disconnect the old client first (lotus-lamp-python documents exactly this failure mode). If the old client is a phone, also remove the device from the OS Bluetooth list so the phone stops auto-reconnecting and holding the link.

variants.notes: Reference unit: live-tested by wporter82/lotus-lamp-python ("MELK-OA10 5F" — note spaces in the advertised name). All E1 commands below verified working on this model by that library; 213 animation modes (0-212).

4th character '*' instead of '-' marks the obfuscated-frame firmware (ON_OFF/MODE/BRIGHTNESS wrapped per the algorithm in device.notes). Other opcodes stay plaintext per static analysis — needs live verification.

variants.model: OEM rebrands (HX6-, HCW-, BYC-, SHY-, MHRS-, THUNDEROBOT, ...)
variants.notes: Same app, same protocol. The app's name matcher also accepts the substrings "LED LIGHT STRIP" and "LED Constellation Lights".

set_animation.description: Set animation/mode 0-212 (cmd 0x03). The full 213-mode table with official names and 8 categories (basic, trans, tail, water, curtain, run, runback, flow) is published in wporter82/lotus-lamp-python. Mode numbers may vary by model.

set_brightness.description: Set brightness 0-100 (cmd 0x01). The app emits len byte 0x04 here (0x07 also accepted on tested hardware — see notes).

set_color.description: Set static RGB color (cmd 0x05, palette type 0x03). The 0x10 in byte 7 is what the app emits for this command.

set_timer.description: Schedule an on/off timer (cmd 0x82, TIMER_SWITCH): hours, minutes, then 0x00, timer_type (0 = switch-on timer, 1 = switch-off timer), and a days bitmask — bit7 set enables the schedule, bits 0-6 are Monday..Sunday.

sync_time.description: Sync the lamp's clock (cmd 0x83, DATA_TIME): hours, minutes, seconds, weekday (1=Monday .. 7=Sunday).

characteristics.name: Command Write
characteristics.notes: Write characteristic for every command. E1 frames below are complete packets written verbatim. The <len> byte (byte 1) is emitted as the app does (4 for brightness, 6 for time sync, else 7) but live testing by lotus-lamp-python shows a MELK-OA10 tolerates other values — do not treat a mismatch as fatal. Confidence: power/color/brightness/speed/mode HIGH (corroborated live); time sync and timer MEDIUM (static analysis only).

characteristics.name: State Notify
characteristics.notes: State notifications. The app subscribes here on connect; the lamp pushes status echoes in the same 7E..EF framing (and the reply to INFO, cmd 0x84). Exact payload semantics are NOT fully mapped — capture live traffic before relying on readback. Confidence: framing MEDIUM, payload layout LOW.

services.name: LotusLamp X Control Service
services.notes: Single custom service: write characteristic 0xFFF3 (write-without-response) for all commands, notify characteristic 0xFFF4 for state echoes. All E1-family writes are complete 9-byte frames (7E <len> <cmd> <4-5 params> EF) — no characteristic-level framing is declared on purpose, exactly as in elk-bledom-led-strip.yaml: a consumer must not prepend length or append a checksum to the values/templates below.
